# Abstract {.unnumbered}


# Introduction

The classification of peripheral blood cells is a fundamental task in haematology, and the starting diagnostic step of 80% of haematological diseases [@acevedo2019recognition]. Manual classification methods that are prone to inter-observer variability [@fan2024microscope; @schelonka1995differentiation] have been gradually replaced by automated methods with the advent of classical and deep machine learning, with different approaches and philosophies emerging. One approach is radiomics inspired, relying on classical computer vision to engineer handcrafted features guided by haematological expertise [@tavakoli2021new], often with the benefit of requiring comparatively less computational resources that is well-suited for low resource settings. A second approach is leveraging pretrained models as backbones, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs), to extract learned features that can be fed into classifiers [@acevedo2019recognition], with this paradigm further expanding with the emergence of domain-specific foundational models such as DinoBloom [@koch2024dinobloom]. Finally, there is the end-to-end fine-tuning approach that optimises the entire model for blood cell classification [@asghar2024classification], a method requiring substantial computational resources from graphics processing units (GPUs). 

Commercial automated analysers are available, but their high cost and closed-source nature limit their accessibility, particularly in low-resource settings [@fan2024microscope; @kratz2019digital]. With nearly half (47%) of the world population lacking access to diagnostics [@fleming2021lancet], there is a need for affordable, open-source solutions regardless of the technological approach. This study compares the three abovementioned approaches on the recently released KU-Optofil dataset [@yarikan2026largescale], evaluating their performance and trade-offs, and validating the models on an external dataset from another centre [@acevedo2020dataset].

# Methods

## Dataset

The [KU-Optofil dataset](https://zenodo.org/records/17333317) [@yarikan2026largescale] contains 31,484 images of peripheral blood cells of 13 classes, from 276 patients. The images are stained using the May-Grünwald-Giemsa method and collected with the Sysmex DI-60 system, and the 13 classes are band neutrophils, basophils, blasts, eosinophils, erythroblasts, giant platelets, lymphocytes, metamyelocytes, monocytes, myelocytes, platelet clusters, reactive lymphocytes, and segmented neutrophils [@fig-eda]a. The metadata provided patient level splits of training (193 patients, 23,057 images), validation (27 patients, 2,662 images) and test (56 patients, 5,765 images), the implementation of which prevented patient level leakage. The images, sized 368 × 368 pixels, were labelled by two expert haematologists with a third expert resolving disagreements, with all classes achieving a Cohen's kappa (κ) of at least 0.85, most classes ≥ 0.94, and several classes in perfect agreement (κ = 1.00). There is however a severe class imbalance [@fig-eda]b, with segmented neutrophils making up more than half of the dataset (51.6%) and lymphocytes (18.3%), while band neutrophils (0.6%), metamyelocytes (0.8%), and myelocytes (0.3%), and erythroblasts (0.8%) each represent less than 1%.

```{python}
    n_classes, 2, figure=fig,
    width_ratios=[1, 4],
    wspace=0.35, hspace=0.12,

for i, cls in enumerate(CLASS_ORDER):
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, 0])
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)

    cls_df = df_meta[df_meta["cell_type"] == cls]
    sample = cls_df.sample(n=1, random_state=42).iloc[0]
    split = sample["path"].split("/")[0]
    class_folder = FOLDER_NAME_MAP[sample["cell_type"]]
    img_path = image_root / split / class_folder / sample["image_name"]
    if img_path.exists():
        ax.imshow(Image.open(img_path))

                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8, color="grey")

# ── Panel (b): horizontal bar chart aligned to image rows ─────────────────
# Single axes spanning all rows; we position bars at the vertical centres
# of the corresponding image axes so alignment is exact.
ax_bar = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 1])

vals = counts.values
bar_labels = [FULL_NAMES[c] for c in counts.index]

# Compute y-positions from image-axis centres (in figure coords → bar data coords)
fig.canvas.draw()  # force layout so positions are resolved
img_centres_fig = []
for i in range(n_classes):
    pos = gs[i, 0].get_position(fig)
    img_centres_fig.append((pos.y0 + pos.y1) / 2)

# Map figure y-coords to bar axes data coords
bar_pos = ax_bar.get_position()
y_data = []
for yf in img_centres_fig:
    # figure coords → axes fraction → data coords
    frac = (yf - bar_pos.y0) / bar_pos.height
    y_data.append(frac)

# Use axes-fraction coordinates directly: set y-axis limits to [0, 1]
ax_bar.set_ylim(0, 1)
bar_height = 0.8 / n_classes

bars = ax_bar.barh(
    y_data, vals,
    color=OI_BLUE, edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.5, height=bar_height,
)

ax_bar.set_yticks(y_data)
ax_bar.set_yticklabels(bar_labels, fontsize=7)
ax_bar.set_xlabel("Number of images", fontsize=8)
ax_bar.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=7)

# Percentage labels at end of each bar
for bar, val in zip(bars, vals):
    pct = val / total * 100
    ax_bar.text(
        bar.get_width() + total * 0.005,
        bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2,
        f"{int(val):,} ({pct:.1f}%)",
        ha="left", va="center", fontsize=6,
    )

# Extend x-axis to fit labels
ax_bar.set_xlim(0, max(vals) * 1.28)

# Panel labels
fig.text(0.01, 0.995, "(a)", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold", va="top")
fig.text(gs[0, 1].get_position(fig).x0, 0.995, "(b)",
         fontsize=10, fontweight="bold", va="top")

plt.show()
```

![Modelling pipeline. Input images are processed through three parallel paths: (i) frozen pretrained backbones producing learned feature vectors, (ii) handcrafted morphological feature extraction using cell segmentation, and (iii) end-to-end fine-tuning. Paths (i) and (ii) feed the same lightweight classifiers.](flowchart@3x.png){#fig-pipeline width=100%}



## Feature Extraction and Classification

Four pretrained deep learning models were used as feature extractors. Two CNNs, ResNet-50 (2048 dimensions) and EfficientNet-B0 (1280 dimensions) were chosen as baseline general-purpose informed feature extractors. DinoBloom-S (384 dimensions), a ViT-based foundational model self-supervised on haematological images [@koch2024dinobloom] was chosen as the domain-informed feature extractor. Finally, to provide a non-domain specific ViT baseline, the ViT-S/16 (384 dimensions) of the same ViT family as DinoBloom-S was used. All images were resized to 224 × 224 pixels and normalised with ImageNet statistics.

To create handcrafted features, 65 morphological features were engineered based on existing literature [@tavakoli2021new; @dasariraju2020detection]. These features were created using the ratios in sizes, colours and textures (grey level co-occurrence matrix: GLCM) between cell, cytoplasm and the nucleus, along with shape metrics such as circularity and solidity. To obtain these ratios, the nucleus and the cell both required segmentation. The nucleus was segmented using the same multi-Otsu thresholding method throughout, while the cell was segmented using two approaches: the convex hull of the nucleus [@tavakoli2021new] and the CellPose SAM model [@pachitariu2025cellpose]. Both approaches were used as the convex hull method is computationally cheaper but could provide a coarser segmentation of the cell, while the CellPose SAM model is more computationally expensive but could provide more accurate cell segmentation. This created two models with handcrafted features, which along with four pretrained backbone models, were fed into the same classifiers below for direct comparisons of the feature extraction methods.

Two classifiers were used on the features generated by the abovementioned feature extractors: XGBoost using Optuna [@akiba2019optuna] via the tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) to tune nine hyperparameters with 100 trials; linear probe using logistic regression with L2 regularisation. XGBoost was chosen for its native multiclass support, ability to learn non-linear interactions and CPU-computation support; linear probe is used as a baseline. Another two models were fine-tuned end-to-end using the ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0 backbones, using Optuna with TPE again for 30 trials with HyperbandPruner for hyperparameter tuning, with a maximum of 50 epochs and early stopping. All three approaches are visualised in the [@fig-pipeline] flowchart.

To account for the class imbalance within the dataset, all classifiers used inverse-frequency class weighting to ensure consistent handling of this severe imbalance across all paradigms, and the macro F1 score was used as the optimisation metric for all hyperparameter tuning.

## Evaluation

As with hyperparameter tuning, the macro F1 score was the primary evaluation metric, as it is sensitive to rare-class performance. Accuracy and weighted F1 score were also reported for literature comparability. XGBoost and fine-tuned models were evaluated across five different random seeds for stability; linear probes are deterministic and require no seed variation. All metrics are reported in [@tbl-main]. For model-model comparison, deltas (Δ) in macro F1 were bootstrapped with 2,000 resamples to obtain 95% confidence intervals (CIs), along with Holm-corrected p-values from McNemar's test.

An [external dataset](https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/snkd93bnjr/1) from Acevedo et al. [@acevedo2020dataset] containing 17,092 images with eight classes obtained via the CellaVision DM96 system and stained with May-Grünwald-Giemsa was used for external validation. Six shared classes between KU-Optofil and Acevedo were evaluated, with "neutrophil" in Acevedo mapped to "segmented neutrophil" in KU-Optofil, and immature granulocytes and platelets dropped. Classifiers were re-trained on KU-Optofil restricted to the six shared classes, reusing best hyperparameters from the 13-class tuning; no Acevedo data was used for training.

## Reproducibility and Hardware

The code for this project is available on GitHub in this [repository](https://github.com/joelyu/HDS-W5.git). Package versions are listed in `requirements.txt`. An anaconda environment can be created with `conda env create -f environment.yml` as well, and the `run_all.sh` script can be used to run all scripts in the correct order. Datasets and model weights are auto-downloaded via scripts from Zenodo, Mendeley, Hugging Face and torchvision.

All models except the fine-tuned models were trained on an M4 Max Mac Studio with 14-core CPU, 32-core GPU, 36GB RAM. The fine-tuned models were trained on the University of Cambridge CSD3 cluster on NVIDIA A100 GPUs, with a 12-hour wall-time limit.

# Results

```{python}
#| label: tbl-main
#| tbl-cap: "Classification performance on the KU-Optofil test set (13-class). XGBoost and end-to-end fine-tuned models report mean ± SD across 5 seeds. Best results for each metric are bolded."

import json

# ── Load results ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
with open(RESULTS_DIR / "xgboost_results.json") as f:
    xgb = json.load(f)
with open(RESULTS_DIR / "linear_probe_results.json") as f:
    lp = json.load(f)
with open(RESULTS_DIR / "finetune_results.json") as f:
    ft = json.load(f)

# ── Define rows ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# (display_name, json_key, classifier)
frozen_rows = [
    ("DinoBloom-S (ViT)",        "dinobloom_s"),
    ("EfficientNet-B0 (CNN)",    "efficientnet_b0"),
    ("Handcrafted (CellPose)",   "handcrafted_cellpose"),
    ("Handcrafted (convex hull)","handcrafted"),
    ("ViT-S/16 (ViT)",          "vit_s16"),
    ("ResNet-50 (CNN)",          "resnet50"),
]

ft_rows = [
    ("ResNet-50 (fine-tuned)",       "resnet50"),
    ("EfficientNet-B0 (fine-tuned)", "efficientnet_b0"),
]

def fmt(val, std=None, bold=False):
    s = f"{val:.3f}"
    if std is not None and std > 0:
        s += f" ± {std:.3f}"
    if bold:
        s = f"**{s}**"
    return s

# ── Build long-format rows ────────────────────────────────────────────────
table_rows = []
for name, key in frozen_rows:
    xt = xgb[key]["test_results"]
    lt = lp[key]["test_results"]
    table_rows.append({"name": name, "classifier": "XGBoost",
        "mf1": xt["macro_f1_mean"], "mf1_std": xt["macro_f1_std"],
        "acc": xt["accuracy_mean"], "wf1": xt["weighted_f1_mean"], "ft": False})
    table_rows.append({"name": name, "classifier": "Linear probe",
        "mf1": lt["macro_f1_mean"], "mf1_std": None,
        "acc": lt["accuracy_mean"], "wf1": lt["weighted_f1_mean"], "ft": False})

for name, key in ft_rows:
    ftt = ft[key]["test_results"]
    table_rows.append({"name": name, "classifier": "End-to-end",
        "mf1": ftt["macro_f1_mean"], "mf1_std": ftt.get("macro_f1_std", None),
        "acc": ftt["accuracy_mean"], "wf1": ftt["weighted_f1_mean"], "ft": True})

# ── Find best values (frozen only) for bolding ────────────────────────────
frozen = [r for r in table_rows if not r["ft"]]
best_mf1 = max(r["mf1"] for r in frozen)
best_acc = max(r["acc"] for r in frozen)
best_wf1 = max(r["wf1"] for r in frozen)

# ── Build markdown table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
header = "| Feature source | Classifier | Macro F1 | Accuracy | Weighted F1 |"
sep =    "|:---|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|"
lines = [header, sep]

prev_name = None
for r in table_rows:
    # Add separator before fine-tuning section
    if r["ft"] and prev_name is not None and not any(
        rr["ft"] for rr in table_rows[:table_rows.index(r)]):
        lines.append("| **End-to-end fine-tuning** | | | | |")

    # Use empty string for repeated backbone names
    display_name = r["name"] if r["name"] != prev_name else ""
    prev_name = r["name"]

    cols = [
        display_name,
        r["classifier"],
        fmt(r["mf1"], r["mf1_std"], r["mf1"] == best_mf1 and not r["ft"]),
        fmt(r["acc"], bold=r["acc"] == best_acc and not r["ft"]),
        fmt(r["wf1"], bold=r["wf1"] == best_wf1 and not r["ft"]),
    ]
    lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cols) + " |")

from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

```{python}
# Horizontal colourbar below the "Predicted" label

cbar = fig.colorbar(im, cax=cbar_ax, orientation="horizontal")
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-umap
#| fig-cap: "UMAP embeddings of test-set features (n = 5,765) in KU-Optofil dataset, coloured by cell class. (a) DinoBloom-S, (b) EfficientNet-B0, (c) ResNet-50."

import umap

# ── Load test features for the three backbones ────────────────────────────
umap_backbones = [
    ("(a) DinoBloom-S",    "dinobloom_s"),
    ("(b) EfficientNet-B0","efficientnet_b0"),
    ("(c) ResNet-50",      "resnet50"),
]

umap_params = dict(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, metric="euclidean", random_state=42)

# Class labels (alphabetical encoding matches the feature NPZs)
UMAP_CLASS_NAMES = [
    "Band Neutrophil", "Basophil", "Blast", "Eosinophil", "Erythroblast",
    "Giant Platelet", "Lymphocyte", "Metamyelocyte", "Monocyte", "Myelocyte",
    "Platelet Cluster", "Reactive Lymphocyte", "Segmented Neutrophil",
]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7, 3.0))

for idx, (ax, (title, backbone)) in enumerate(zip(axes, umap_backbones)):
    feat = np.load(RESULTS_DIR / f"{backbone}_features.npz", allow_pickle=True)
    X_test = feat["test_X"]
    y_raw = feat["test_y"]
    # Labels may be strings or ints — map to int indices
    if y_raw.dtype.kind in ("U", "S", "O"):  # string types
        from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
        le = LabelEncoder()
        le.fit(sorted(set(y_raw)))
        y_test = le.transform(y_raw)
    else:
        y_test = y_raw.astype(int)

    reducer = umap.UMAP(**umap_params)
    embedding = reducer.fit_transform(X_test)

    for cls_idx in range(len(UMAP_CLASS_NAMES)):
        mask = y_test == cls_idx
        if mask.sum() == 0:
            continue
        ax.scatter(
            embedding[mask, 0], embedding[mask, 1],
            color=CLASS_COLOURS[cls_idx], s=1, alpha=0.8,
            edgecolors="none", linewidths=0,
            label=UMAP_CLASS_NAMES[cls_idx] if idx == 0 else None,
        )

    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=7, pad=4)
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.set_xlim(embedding[:, 0].min() - 1, embedding[:, 0].max() + 1)
    ax.set_ylim(embedding[:, 1].min() - 1, embedding[:, 1].max() + 1)
    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)

# Shared legend below all panels
handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(
    handles, labels, loc="lower center",
    ncol=4, fontsize=5, markerscale=4,
    frameon=False, handletextpad=0.3, columnspacing=1.0,
)

plt.subplots_adjust(left=0.01, right=0.99, bottom=0.15, top=0.93, wspace=0.05)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-attention
#| fig-cap: "DinoBloom-S attention visualisations for 13 classes. Left: original image (resized to 224 × 224). Centre: PCA of patch tokens, top 3 components mapped to red, green and blue colors. Right: token-norm heatmap (brighter = higher activation)."

import os
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"
os.environ["KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK"] = "TRUE"

import torch
import torchvision.transforms as T
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA

# Load DinoBloom-S
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

model = torch.hub.load("facebookresearch/dinov2", "dinov2_vits14", verbose=False)
ckpt_path = hf_hub_download(repo_id="MarrLab/DinoBloom", filename="pytorch_model_s.bin")
ckpt = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
num_tokens = int(1 + (224 / 14) ** 2)
model.pos_embed = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, num_tokens, 384))
model.load_state_dict(ckpt, strict=True)
model.eval()

device = torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")
model.to(device)

transform = T.Compose([
    T.Resize((224, 224)),
    T.ToTensor(),
    T.Normalize(mean=[0.485, 0.456, 0.406], std=[0.229, 0.224, 0.225]),
])

# All 13 classes
attn_classes = CLASS_ORDER
samples = []
for cls in attn_classes:
    cls_df = df_meta[df_meta["cell_type"] == cls]
    row = cls_df.sample(n=1, random_state=42).iloc[0]
    class_folder = FOLDER_NAME_MAP[row["cell_type"]]
    split = row["path"].split("/")[0]
    img_path = image_root / split / class_folder / row["image_name"]
    if img_path.exists():
        samples.append((FULL_NAMES[cls], img_path))

patch_size = 14
grid_size = 224 // patch_size

# ── 2-column layout: 7 rows left, 6 rows right ──────────────────────────
# Each "column" has 3 sub-columns: original | PCA | token norms
# Total grid columns: 3 (left) + gap + 3 (right) = 7
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec

n_left = 7
n_right = len(samples) - n_left  # 6
n_rows = max(n_left, n_right)

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(7, 0.9 * n_rows))
gs = gridspec.GridSpec(
    n_rows, 7, figure=fig,
    width_ratios=[1, 1, 1, 0.8, 1, 1, 1],
    wspace=0, hspace=0.25,
    left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.95, bottom=0.01,
)

def render_sample(fig, gs_row, gs_col_offset, cls_name, img_path, show_title):
    """Render one sample: original | PCA | token norms into 3 grid cells."""
    img_pil = Image.open(img_path).convert("RGB")
    img_resized = img_pil.resize((224, 224))
    img_tensor = transform(img_pil).unsqueeze(0).to(device)

    with torch.no_grad():
        tokens = model.get_intermediate_layers(img_tensor, n=1)[0]
        n_tokens = tokens.shape[1]
        if n_tokens == grid_size * grid_size + 1:
            patch_tokens = tokens[0, 1:, :].cpu().numpy()
        else:
            patch_tokens = tokens[0, :, :].cpu().numpy()

    # PCA → RGB
    pca = PCA(n_components=3)
    pca_result = pca.fit_transform(patch_tokens)
    for c in range(3):
        mn, mx = pca_result[:, c].min(), pca_result[:, c].max()
        if mx > mn:
            pca_result[:, c] = (pca_result[:, c] - mn) / (mx - mn)
    pca_image = pca_result.reshape(grid_size, grid_size, 3)

    # Token norms
    token_norms_val = np.linalg.norm(patch_tokens, axis=1)
    norm_map = token_norms_val.reshape(grid_size, grid_size)
    norm_map = (norm_map - norm_map.min()) / (norm_map.max() - norm_map.min() + 1e-8)

    for j, (img_data, cmap, title) in enumerate([
        (img_resized, None, "Original"),
        (pca_image, None, "Patch PCA"),
        (norm_map, "inferno", "Token norms"),
    ]):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[gs_row, gs_col_offset + j])
        if cmap:
            ax.imshow(img_data, cmap=cmap)
        else:
            ax.imshow(img_data)
        ax.set_xticks([])
        ax.set_yticks([])
        for spine in ax.spines.values():
            spine.set_visible(False)
        if show_title:
            ax.set_title(title, fontsize=5, pad=2)
        if j == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel(cls_name, fontsize=5, rotation=0, ha="right", va="center", labelpad=3)

# Left column: first 7 classes
for i in range(n_left):
    cls_name, img_path = samples[i]
    render_sample(fig, i, 0, cls_name, img_path, show_title=(i == 0))

# Right column: remaining 6 classes
for i in range(n_right):
    cls_name, img_path = samples[n_left + i]
    render_sample(fig, i, 4, cls_name, img_path, show_title=(i == 0))

# Bottom-right cell is empty (6 vs 7) — leave blank

plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-external
#| tbl-cap: "Classification performance on the Acevedo external validation set (6-class). XGBoost rows report mean ± SD across 5 seeds; fine-tuned models were not validated. Best values per metric are bolded."

import json

with open(RESULTS_DIR / "external_validation.json") as f:
    ext = json.load(f)

ext_backbones = [
    ("DinoBloom-S (ViT)",        "dinobloom_s"),
    ("EfficientNet-B0 (CNN)",    "efficientnet_b0"),
    ("Handcrafted (CellPose)",   "handcrafted_cellpose"),
    ("Handcrafted (convex hull)","handcrafted"),
    ("ViT-S/16 (ViT)",          "vit_s16"),
    ("ResNet-50 (CNN)",          "resnet50"),
]

def fmt_ext(val, std=None, bold=False):
    s = f"{val:.3f}"
    if std is not None and std > 0:
        s += f" ± {std:.3f}"
    if bold:
        s = f"**{s}**"
    return s

table_rows = []
for name, key in ext_backbones:
    for clf_key, clf_name in [("xgboost", "XGBoost"), ("linear", "Linear probe")]:
        seeds = ext[key][clf_key]["per_seed"]
        mf1s = [s["macro_f1"] for s in seeds]
        accs = [s["accuracy"] for s in seeds]
        wf1s = [s["weighted_f1"] for s in seeds]
        mf1_mean = np.mean(mf1s)
        mf1_std = np.std(mf1s) if len(seeds) > 1 and clf_key == "xgboost" else None
        table_rows.append({
            "name": name, "classifier": clf_name,
            "mf1": mf1_mean, "mf1_std": mf1_std,
            "acc": np.mean(accs), "wf1": np.mean(wf1s),
        })

best_mf1 = max(r["mf1"] for r in table_rows)
best_acc = max(r["acc"] for r in table_rows)
best_wf1 = max(r["wf1"] for r in table_rows)

header = "| Feature source | Classifier | Macro F1 | Accuracy | Weighted F1 |"
sep =    "|:---|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|"
lines = [header, sep]

prev_name = None
for r in table_rows:
    display_name = r["name"] if r["name"] != prev_name else ""
    prev_name = r["name"]
    cols = [
        display_name,
        r["classifier"],
        fmt_ext(r["mf1"], r["mf1_std"], r["mf1"] == best_mf1),
        fmt_ext(r["acc"], bold=r["acc"] == best_acc),
        fmt_ext(r["wf1"], bold=r["wf1"] == best_wf1),
    ]
    lines.append("| " + " | ".join(cols) + " |")

from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-segmentation-comparison
#| fig-cap: "Cell segmentation comparison for six representative cell types. Each row shows (left to right): the original image; nucleus mask from multi-Otsu thresholding (white); convex hull cell boundary (green outline — the convex envelope of the nucleus); and CellPose cell boundary (green outline)."

from segmentation import segment_nucleus, cell_mask_convex_hull
import cv2

# Pick one representative image per class (diverse morphologies)
seg_classes = ["eosinophil", "lymphocyte", "monocyte", "blast", "segmented_neutrophil", "erythroblast"]

seg_samples = []
for cls in seg_classes:
    cls_df = df_meta[df_meta["cell_type"] == cls]
    row = cls_df.sample(n=1, random_state=42).iloc[0]
    class_folder = FOLDER_NAME_MAP[row["cell_type"]]
    split = row["path"].split("/")[0]
    img_path = image_root / split / class_folder / row["image_name"]
    if img_path.exists():
        seg_samples.append((FULL_NAMES[cls], row["image_name"], img_path))

n_samples = len(seg_samples)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_samples, 4, figsize=(7, 1.6 * n_samples))

for row_idx, (cls_name, img_name, img_path) in enumerate(seg_samples):
    img = cv2.imread(str(img_path))
    img_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

    # Nucleus segmentation (same for both methods)
    nuc_mask, _ = segment_nucleus(img_rgb)

    # Convex hull cell mask
    cvx_mask = cell_mask_convex_hull(nuc_mask)

    # CellPose mask
    cp_path = RESULTS_DIR / "cellpose_masks" / f"{img_name}.png"
    if cp_path.exists():
        cp_mask = np.array(Image.open(cp_path).convert("L")) > 0
    else:
        cp_mask = cvx_mask  # fallback

    # Column 0: original
    axes[row_idx, 0].imshow(img_rgb)
    axes[row_idx, 0].set_ylabel(cls_name, fontsize=6, rotation=0, ha="right", va="center", labelpad=3)

    # Column 1: nucleus mask overlay
    overlay_nuc = img_rgb.copy()
    overlay_nuc[nuc_mask > 0] = (overlay_nuc[nuc_mask > 0] * 0.5 + np.array([255, 255, 255]) * 0.5).astype(np.uint8)
    axes[row_idx, 1].imshow(overlay_nuc)

    # Column 2: convex hull outline
    overlay_cvx = img_rgb.copy()
    cvx_contours, _ = cv2.findContours(cvx_mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    cv2.drawContours(overlay_cvx, cvx_contours, -1, (0, 200, 0), 2)
    nuc_contours, _ = cv2.findContours(nuc_mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    cv2.drawContours(overlay_cvx, nuc_contours, -1, (255, 255, 255), 1)
    axes[row_idx, 2].imshow(overlay_cvx)

    # Column 3: CellPose outline
    overlay_cp = img_rgb.copy()
    cp_contours, _ = cv2.findContours(cp_mask.astype(np.uint8), cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
    cv2.drawContours(overlay_cp, cp_contours, -1, (0, 200, 0), 2)
    cv2.drawContours(overlay_cp, nuc_contours, -1, (255, 255, 255), 1)
    axes[row_idx, 3].imshow(overlay_cp)

    for col in range(4):
        axes[row_idx, col].set_xticks([])
        axes[row_idx, col].set_yticks([])
        for spine in axes[row_idx, col].spines.values():
            spine.set_visible(False)

# Column titles
for col, title in enumerate(["Original", "Nucleus mask", "Convex hull", "CellPose"]):
    axes[0, col].set_title(title, fontsize=7, pad=4)

plt.subplots_adjust(left=0.15, right=0.98, bottom=0.01, top=0.95, wspace=0.05, hspace=0.15)
plt.show()
```
